topic: Measurements of lift and drag in wind tunnel.
syllabus_extract: Measurements of lift and drag in wind tunnel.
specific_objectives: 6.1.5 .1Trainee will be able to explain about wind tunnel operation

training_aids.remarks: Refer to the master syllabus reference list
Objective: teach the syllabus extract for this lesson

practical: Wind tunnel model mounting, balance calibration, and force reading recording. Safety: Secure model fixation, check fan clearance. Instructor supervision: Continuous monitoring of balance readings.
intro_questions: What is the primary purpose of a wind tunnel in aerodynamics?
Define lift and drag forces acting on an aircraft.
How does airspeed affect the magnitude of aerodynamic forces?

development.content:
Wind tunnel operational principles
Force balance systems overview
Calibration of measurement instruments

Lift measurement techniques
Drag measurement techniques
Data acquisition and recording

Error sources in force measurement
Correction factors application
Interpretation of test results

summary_questions: Explain the difference between direct and indirect drag measurement methods.
How does model support interference affect lift and drag readings?
Calculate the lift coefficient given force, dynamic pressure, and area.
home_assignment_question: Research the types of strain gauge balances used in modern wind tunnels and their advantages over mechanical balances.
